name: Question 9
problem: A particle $P$ moves along the positive $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $k\sqrt{x}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant. If $P$ has velocity $v=6\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has velocity $v=6\sqrt{6}\,m/s$ when its displacement is $9\,m,$ find the value of $k.$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094268/assets/b052a65fb0dbcc14a5d359b693beafdf5da3f4bbe1e10f006c315e8168340d5c.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $k\sqrt{x}\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=k\sqrt{x}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=k\sqrt{x}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (k\sqrt{x})\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{2k}{3}{x}^{3/2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=6\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{2k}{3}{x}^{3/2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(6)^{2} & =\frac{2k}{3}(0)^{3/2}+C \\ C & =18\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{2k}{3}{x}^{3/2}+18.
$$

Finally, since $v=6\sqrt{6}\,m/s$ when $x=9\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{2k}{3}{x}^{3/2}+18 \\ \frac{1}{2}(6\sqrt{6})^{2} & =\frac{2k}{3}(9)^{3/2}+18 \\ 108 & =18k+18 \\ 18k & =90 \\ k & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

A particle P moves along the positive x-axis. When the displacement of P from the origin is xm, the velocity is vm/s, and the acceleration is kxm/s2, where k is a positive constant. If P has velocity v=6m/s at the origin and the particle has velocity v=66m/s when its displacement is 9m, find the value of k.

a

b
 8
c
 3
d
 5
e
 34
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the acceleration of the particle P is kxm/s2, we have

dvdt=kx.

Using the fact that dvdt=ddx(12v2), we can rewrite our equation as

ddx(12v2)=kx.

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to x, we have

∫ddx(12v2)dx=∫(kx)dx

which gives the general solution

12v2=2k3x3/2+C.

Now, since v=6m/s when x=0m, we can find the value of the constant C, as follows:

12v2=2k3x3/2+C12(6)2=2k3(0)3/2+CC=18

Therefore,

12v2=2k3x3/2+18.

Finally, since v=66m/s when x=9m, we can find the value of the positive constant k, as follows:

12v2=2k3x3/2+1812(66)2=2k3(9)3/2+18108=18k+1818k=90k=5.
